sourceIssues.correction: In the bad-type clauses of Theorems 1.2 and 4.8, replace the claimed limit by liminf, retaining all group, characteristic and sufficiently-large-n hypotheses. This finding does not exhibit a group for which that limit actually fails to exist.

sourceIssues.locator: Definition 3.12, arXiv 1702.04644v2 p.13 / published p.394; proof of Theorem 3.13, v2 p.14 / published pp.395–396. Both versions independently collated.
sourceIssues.printed: "Let Γ be the tame quotient of G_{F̄_p(t)} corresponding to extensions only ramified at S. Then Γ is free pro-prime-to-p, on generators δ_1, …, δ_k, with each generator generating the tame inertia subgroup at a point of S∖∞."
sourceIssues.correction: Let Γ be the maximal prime-to-p quotient of that tame quotient. This Γ is free pro-prime-to-p on δ_1, …, δ_k with δ_1⋯δ_kδ_∞ = 1. Since |F| is prime to p, φ factors through it.
sourceIssues.reason: Independently checked both versions and SGA 1 XIII Corollary 2.12, including its proof: the single-relation free presentation is asserted for the maximal prime-to-p quotient, not an identification of the entire tame group with that quotient. A concrete tame quotient of order divisible by p is given by the characteristic-3 elliptic example in the review: E:y²=x³+x²+1 has a point P=(2,1) of order 3, and translations by P together with inversion give a tame S3-cover of P¹, branched at four points with inertia order 2. This also fits a branch set arising from a prime-to-3 quadratic cover. Replaced the inherited modular-cover assertion by this independently checked example. Since |F| is prime to p, both F and its reduced Schur cover have prime-to-p order (the Schur multiplier is finite and annihilated by |F|). Thus the homomorphisms used in the definition and lifting argument factor through the corrected quotient. Confirmed the slip without claiming a failure of the intended invariant.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 4.4 and proof, arXiv 1702.04644v2 pp.19–20 / published pp.402–403. Both versions independently collated.
sourceIssues.printed: "Let Q be a global field with a choice of place ∞. Let G be a finite group and G′ a subgroup of G ≀ S_2. Let c be the order 2 elements of G′ with non-trivial image in S_2. Let φ: Gal(Q̄_∞/Q_∞) → G′ be a ramified homomorphism with image ⟨(1,σ)⟩. There is a bijection between {(K,ρ) | … ρ ∈ Sur(G_K^{un,∞}, G) | ρ is type G′} and {isomorphism classes of marked (G′,c) extensions (L,π,m) of Q with infinity type φ}." The proof builds ρ from a marked extension "by projection onto the first factor" and says "It is straightforward to check that these constructions are inverses to each other".
sourceIssues.correction: Assume G′ is admissible. For the inverse-construction issue, a weaker sufficient condition is (1,σ)∈G′ together with surjectivity of ker(G′→S2) onto the first factor G; the ramified infinity-type hypothesis already implies the former in the first bijection. The swap then also gives surjectivity onto the second factor, and the intersection of the projection kernels is trivial. The applications in Theorem 4.8 use admissible G′.
sourceIssues.reason: Read both bijections and their inverse construction in both versions. For G=C3 and G′=⟨(1,σ)⟩≅C2, the marked imaginary quadratic extension Q(√−3)/Q gives a point on the right of the first bijection, with the required infinity type and allowed finite inertia. The left side is empty because a C3-extension of a quadratic field has degree 6 over Q, so its Galois closure cannot have group of order 2. The inverse projection from ker(G′→S2)=1 is not surjective. Confirmed the missing hypothesis. The correction below includes (1,σ)∈G′ explicitly when giving the weaker alternative, rather than treating surjectivity of one projection alone as all the needed data. With those assumptions, the two projection kernels intersect trivially, so the two conjugate subextensions recover M; the inertia conditions give the required unramified extension.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 4.8, real quadratic case, arXiv 1702.04644v2 p.25 / published pp.409–410 (the incorrect discriminant sentence is on p.409). Both versions independently collated.
sourceIssues.printed: "Note that trivial infinity type φ is exactly what makes the associated quadratic extension real quadratic (this was the definition of real quadratic). In particular these extensions have Nm Disc(M) = q^{(Σ_i n_i+1)|G′|/2}, and thus associated quadratic extension with discriminant norm q^{Σ_i n_i+1},"
sourceIssues.correction: Nm Disc(M) = q^{(Σ_i n_i)|G′|/2}, and the associated quadratic extension has discriminant norm q^{Σ_i n_i}.
sourceIssues.reason: With trivial infinity type, the place at infinity is unramified and contributes nothing to the discriminant. The paper's own convention before Theorem 4.8 is Σ n_i = 2n − ε, with ε = 0 when K is unramified at infinity. The count that follows is q^{2n} + O_n(q^{2n−1/2}) over RQ_{=q^{2n}}, consistent with Σ n_i = 2n. The sentence was copied from the imaginary case, where the "+1" is correct. Noted by the extraction (item 91).

review.reason: Read the real and imaginary paragraphs side by side in both versions. In the real case infinity splits and contributes zero to the different/discriminant. Every finite inertia group is tame of order 2, so the G′-cover contributes |G′|/2 times the finite branch degree Σn_i, and the quadratic cover contributes Σn_i. Thus both printed +1 terms must be removed. The subsequent count has dimension 2n and denominator q^(2n)−q^(2n−1), consistent with this correction. Confirmed a copied exponent slip; no correction to the imaginary +1.

sourceIssues.locator: Conjecture 5.1, arXiv 1702.04644v2 p.26 / published p.411; Lemma 3.11, v2 p.13 / published p.393. Both versions independently collated.
sourceIssues.printed: "Let h ∈ H_2(G′,c)|μ_Q|. Let u ∈ μ_{Q(μ_{4|G̃′_c|})}. If G′ is good, then lim_{X→∞} (Σ_{K∈IQ^t_X} #{ρ ∈ Sur(G_K^{un,∞}, G) | ρ is type G′, I_{G′,π,Q}(ρ,u) = h}) / (Σ_{K∈IQ^t_X} 1) = 1, and" the same for real quadratic fields.
sourceIssues.correction: Write h∈H_2(G′,c)[|μ_Q|] and take u to be a generator of the cyclic group μ_L, L=Q(μ_(4|G̃′_c|)). Equivalently formulate the conjecture by the Hom-valued invariant. This is a sufficient repair of the indexing: more generally, if u=ζ^a for a generator ζ, evaluation is h↦h^a on H_2(G′,c)[|μ_Q|], so it is enough that this power map be an automorphism. The average-one assertion after this repair remains conjectural.
sourceIssues.reason: Lemma 3.11 with exponent 0, or the homomorphism property immediately after Definition 3.1, gives I(ρ,1)=1. Thus u=1 and h≠1 make the numerator identically zero, contradicting the predicted average 1. The review independently constructs a good admissible F=PSL2(F5)≀C2 with nonzero H2(F,c)[2] using a stem central extension by C2 that kills the c-commutators; this does not rely on trusting the table's computed multiplier. A generator of μ_L is a sufficient clean repair, not a necessary choice in every case: writing u=ζ^a, evaluation is the a-power map on H2(F,c)[|μ_Q|]. Also fixed the inherited claim about printed braces: both page images print juxtaposition H2(G′,c)|μ_Q|, with no torsion brackets. The revised generator formulation remains a conjecture, not a proved average.

sourceIssues.reason: Read the full theoretical-computation paragraph in both versions. The trivial action on (C2×C2)⋊C3 gives C2×C2×C3, of order 12, whereas the twice-printed C3×C3×C2 has order 18. Confirmed both occurrences. In the imaginary quadratic setting of the computation, an unramified abelian extension is stable under conjugation because conjugation acts on the ideal class group by inversion; hence the contextual class-field-theory exclusion remains valid. No general assertion about arbitrary abelian extensions of arbitrary base fields is inferred.
